stories.topicLabel: Democrats win Congress in 2026 midterm elections
stories.analysis: Coverage of Democrats' 2026 midterm victory spanned a wide 6.5-point bias range, with framing diverging sharply depending on outlet orientation. At the left end, HuffPost celebrated a CNN host who "Brutally Trolls Trump," while The Atlantic declared "A Night of Pure Trumpenfreude" and the New York Times described "A Big Blue Bludgeoning" — language that treated the results as cause for open partisan celebration. Center-left outlets like the Guardian and AP settled on phrases such as "strong rebuke" and "blue wave," framing voters as enforcers against Trump without fully abandoning news conventions. Neutral-coded outlets like the Wall Street Journal confined themselves to market movements: "Dow Jumps After Democrats Sweep Congress." On the right, National Review ran analytical self-criticism — "Populism Proves Massively Unpopular" and "Trump Has Been the Author of His Own Ruin" — while The Federalist shifted toward alarm, labeling Democratic investigations "Lawfare" and warning "Here Come the Socialists," treating the same electoral outcome as an ideological threat rather than a democratic result.
